CLKCTRLGeneric Clock Controlp. 96

offset 0x2 · 16 bits · reset 0x0000 · access R/W

  • Write CLKCTRL as one 16-bit access carrying the configuration and ID. To read it, first write the generic clock's ID to CLKCTRL.ID with an 8-bit access, then read CLKCTRL.
BitsFieldAccessResetWhat it does
15WRTLOCKR/W0Writing it locks the generic clock named by CLKCTRL.ID, the generator named by CLKCTRL.GEN and that generator's division factor against further writes, until a power reset. Generic clock generator 0 cannot be locked.
0Generic clock, its generator and division factor unlocked.
1Generic clock, its generator and division factor locked.
14CLKENR/W0Turns the generic clock on or off.
0Generic clock off.
1Generic clock on.
11:8GENR/W0x0Generic clock generator feeding this generic clock.
0x0GCLK0GCLK0.
0x1GCLK1GCLK1.
0x2GCLK2GCLK2.
0x3GCLK3GCLK3.
0x4GCLK4GCLK4.
0x5GCLK5GCLK5.
0x6-0xFReserved.
5:0IDR/W0x0Names the generic clock that the rest of CLKCTRL configures. A power reset returns CLKCTRL to its reset value for every ID, the RTC included; a user reset does so only for an ID other than the RTC whose WRTLOCK is 0. After a power reset GEN, CLKEN and WRTLOCK are 0x00 for every ID except the WDT, whose GEN is 0x02, whose CLKEN follows the WDT Enable bit of the NVM User Row (0x01 when it is one, 0x00 when zero) and whose WRTLOCK follows the WDT Always-On bit of the NVM User Row the same way. After a user reset WRTLOCK never changes; for the RTC, GEN and CLKEN become 0x00 when WRTLOCK and CLKEN are both 0 and are kept otherwise; for the WDT with WRTLOCK at 0, GEN becomes 0x02 and CLKEN follows the WDT Enable bit as after a power reset, and with WRTLOCK at 1 both are kept; for every other ID, GEN and CLKEN become 0x00 when WRTLOCK is 0 and are kept when it is 1.

0x1GCLK_DPLLFDPLL96M reference clock input.
0x2GCLK_DPLL_32KFDPLL96M 32kHz clock for its internal lock timer.

GENCTRLGeneric Clock Generator Controlp. 99

offset 0x4 · 32 bits · reset 0x00000000 · access R/W

  • Write GENCTRL as one 32-bit access carrying the configuration and ID. To read it, first write the generator's ID to GENCTRL.ID with an 8-bit access, then read GENCTRL.
BitsFieldAccessResetWhat it does
21RUNSTDBYR/W0Keeps the generator running in standby when its output goes to its GCLK_IO pin. With GENCTRL.OE at 0 it has no effect, and the generator runs only if a peripheral asks for its clock.
0Generator stops in standby; GCLK_IO level follows GENCTRL.OOV.
1Generator keeps running in standby and drives its GCLK_IO pin.
20DIVSELR/W0Chooses how the generator divides its clock source. For no division, DIVSEL must be 0 and the generator's GENDIV.DIV 0 or 1.
0Source divided by GENDIV.DIV.
1Source divided by 2^(GENDIV.DIV+1).
19OER/W0Sends the generated clock out on GCLK_IO, when GCLK_IO is not chosen as a source in GENCLK.SRC.
0No output.
1Output on its GCLK_IO, unless that GCLK_IO is chosen as a source in GENCLK.SRC.
18OOVR/W0Sets the GCLK_IO pin level for the case where GENCLK.SRC does not pick GCLK_IO as a source.
0GCLK_IO low while the generator is off or OE is 0.
1GCLK_IO high while the generator is off or OE is 0.
17IDCR/W0Makes the generator's duty cycle even when an odd division factor is used.
0Duty cycle uneven for odd division factors.
150/50 duty cycle.
16GENENR/W0Turns the generic clock generator on or off.
0Generator off.
1Generator on.

0x00XOSCXOSC output.

A power reset resets GENCTRL for every ID, the RTC's generator included, to 0x00010600 for generator 0, 0x00010302 for generator 2 and the ID alone (0x0000000n) for generators 1, 3, 4 and 5. A user reset gives generator 0 the same value, and generators 1-5 too unless the RTC clock or a generic clock with WRTLOCK at 1 runs from them, in which case they keep their contents.

GENDIVGeneric Clock Generator Divisionp. 103

offset 0x8 · 32 bits · reset 0x00000000 · access R/W

  • Write GENDIV as one 32-bit access carrying the division factor and ID. To read it, first write the generator's ID to GENDIV.ID with an 8-bit access, then read GENDIV.
BitsFieldAccessResetWhat it does
23:8DIVR/W0x0Division factor for the selected generator. Width depends on the generator: generator 0 has 8 bits (DIV[7:0]), generator 1 has 16 (DIV[15:0]), generator 2 has 5 (DIV[4:0]), generators 3-8 have 8 (DIV[7:0]); writes to higher bits are ignored.
3:0IDR/W0x0Selects the generic clock generator the division factor applies to. A power reset resets GENDIV for every ID, the RTC's generator included, to DIV 0 with the ID (0x0000000n). A user reset does the same for generator 0, and for generators 1-5 unless the RTC clock or a generic clock with WRTLOCK at 1 runs from them, in which case they keep their contents.

0x5GCLKGEN5Generator 5.

0x1X2Next address = address + BEATSIZE x 2.
0x2X4Next address = address + BEATSIZE x 4.

0x1INTBlock interrupt; the channel carries on normally.
0x2SUSPENDThe channel is suspended.
0x3BOTHBlock interrupt and the channel is suspended.

0x1BLOCKEvent strobe at each completed block transfer.
0x2Reserved.
0x3BEATEvent strobe at each completed beat transfer.

CTRLAControl Ap. 361

offset 0x00 · 16 bits · reset 0x0000 · access R/W

BitsFieldAccessResetWhat it does
15:8CMDEXR/W0x0Key that lets the command in CMD run: 0xA5 is the execution key. Any other key blocks the write and sets STATUS.PROGE, which is also set when an earlier command has not finished. Write the key in the same access as CMD, and only while READY is one. When an APB command meets an AHB access in the same cycle, the AHB access goes first and the command runs once the AHB bus and the NVM block are idle. Bit 0 reads one until the command has been issued.
0x0-0xa4Reserved.
0xA5KEYExecution key.
0xa6-0xffReserved.
6:0CMDR/W0x0Selects the command that runs when the CMDEX key is written.
0x0-0x1Reserved.
0x2ERErase Row: erases the row at the address in ADDR.
0x3Reserved.
0x4WPWrite Page: copies the page buffer into the page at the address in ADDR.
0x5EARErase Auxiliary Row: erases the auxiliary row at the address in ADDR; accepted only while the security bit is clear, and only for the user configuration row.
0x6WAPWrite Auxiliary Page: copies the page buffer into the auxiliary page at the address in ADDR; accepted only while the security bit is clear, and only for the user configuration row.
0x7-0x9Reserved.
0xASFSecurity flow command.
0xb-0xeReserved.
0xFWLWrites the lockbits.
0x10-0x3fReserved.
0x40LRLock Region: locks the region holding the address in ADDR.
0x41URUnlock Region: unlocks the region holding the address in ADDR.
0x42SPRMTurns power reduction mode on.
0x43CPRMTurns power reduction mode off.
0x44PBCPage Buffer Clear: empties the page buffer.
0x45SSBSet Security Bit: writes 0x00 to the first byte of the lockbit row, setting the security bit.
0x46INVALLMarks every cache line invalid.
0x47-0x7fReserved.

17:16READMODER/W0x0How the cache handles misses: 0x0 NO_MISS_PENALTY adds no wait states on a miss, for the highest system performance; 0x1 LOW_POWER lowers cache power but adds a wait state on every miss, which stalls the CPU and can lengthen run time; 0x2 DETERMINISTIC makes a hit and a miss take the same time, set by the flash wait states, for code needing fixed timing; 0x3 is reserved.
0x0NO_MISS_PENALTYNo wait state on a cache miss; best system performance.
0x1LOW_POWERLower cache power, with a wait state on every cache miss.

0x1WAKEUPINSTANTLow-power on entering sleep; wakes on leaving sleep.
0x2Reserved.

10:0ADDRR/W0x0Writing an address starts bus activity according to bus state. Unknown: the operation ends at once, with STATUS.BUSERR and INTFLAG.MB set. Busy: the master waits for idle. Idle: the master sends a START and the address; on an ACK it holds SCL low and sets STATUS.CLKHOLD and INTFLAG.MB. Owner: the master sends a repeated START, after first sending the acknowledge action if the last transfer was a read; this is done while INTFLAG.MB or INTFLAG.SB is 1. The whole address is sent whether arbitration is won or lost; after a loss only ones go out. A write clears the flags INTFLAG.SB, INTFLAG.MB, STATUS.ARBLOST and STATUS.BUSERR. Reading ADDR never disturbs the bus. Bit 0 is the R/W bit: 0 write, 1 read.
